description: we are undergraduate students from CUET. Competing  as a Team THEIA, I'm building EchoSphere for the "Dancing with the SARs" challenge in NASA Space Apps 2026. Passionate about satellite remote sensing and radar data analysis.
summary:
Project EchoSphere is an interactive, all-weather geospatial early-warning platform built using NASA-ISRO NISAR L-band Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) data. Every year, devastating floods and riverbank erosion strike floodplains like Bangladesh during peak monsoon seasons, when thick cloud cover blinds traditional optical satellites.

Addressing the Dancing with the SARs challenge, EchoSphere transforms 12-day repeat-pass NISAR Level-2 GCOV backscatter data (via ASF DAAC)—combined with NASA CMR, GIBS IMERG rainfall tiles, NASA POWER, and Open-Meteo—into intuitive visualizations. Users can select any region worldwide to explore interactive before-and-after time-swipe maps, monitor dedicated Flood Watch and Erosion Watch dashboards, and simulate high- or low-risk hazard scenarios.

Crucially, EchoSphere bridges the last-mile communication gap by translating complex radar observations into automated, plain-Bangla emergency SMS alerts for at-risk villages without internet access—making catastrophic floods predictable, preventable, and actionable before disaster strikes.
details:
Project EchoSphere is an all-weather geospatial monitoring and early-warning web application designed for the Dancing with the SARs challenge. Traditional optical satellites fail during peak monsoon seasons because thick storm clouds block visibility when flood and erosion disasters are most active. EchoSphere solves this by harnessing NASA-ISRO NISAR L-band Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) data, whose long microwave pulses penetrate heavy cloud cover, rain, and darkness to capture Earth's surface changes on a consistent 12-day repeat cycle.

Our processing pipeline ingests NISAR Level-2 GCOV (Geocoded Covariance) radar backscatter products from ASF DAAC, queries live orbital passes via NASA CMR, overlays real-time precipitation tiles from NASA GIBS IMERG, and integrates historical and forecast climate telemetry from NASA POWER and Open-Meteo. Through our web interface, users can:

  • Select & Analyze Any Region Worldwide: Search or click any coordinate—from major deltaic floodplains like Bangladesh's Jamuna River to global river basins—to inspect radar backscatter shifts.
  • Interactive 12-Day Time-Swipe Map: Compare before-and-after SAR acquisitions using a split-screen slider to visualize water inundation and riverbank retreat.
  • Flood Watch & Erosion Watch Dashboards: Monitor localized water-mask anomalies, soil saturation, and shoreline displacement metrics.
  • Risk Scenario Simulator: Test high-risk and low-risk flood/erosion thresholds to evaluate community vulnerability under extreme monsoon conditions.
  • Automated Plain-Bangla Emergency SMS Alerts: Translate technical radar anomalies into clear, actionable SMS warnings sent directly to basic mobile phones.

Benefits & Intended Impact

  • Uninterrupted Monsoon Visibility: Eliminates cloud-cover blind spots during critical disaster windows.
  • Last-Mile Inclusion: Vulnerable rural and river-island (char) communities often lack smartphones or high-speed internet. By delivering localized alerts in plain Bangla via standard SMS, EchoSphere ensures life-saving warnings reach everyone—not just technical analysts.
  • Scalable Future Product: Built to scale from a hackathon prototype into a nationwide early-warning infrastructure for Bangladesh and other climate-vulnerable river basins globally.

Tools, Coding Languages & Data Stack

  • NASA & Partner Data: NASA-ISRO NISAR Level-2 GCOV (via ASF DAAC), NASA Common Metadata Repository (CMR), NASA GIBS IMERG, NASA POWER, and Open-Meteo APIs.
  • Backend & Geospatial Processing: Python (process_nisar.py) for SAR radiometric/backscatter analysis, water-mask extraction, and automated alert triggers.
  • Frontend & Mapping Stack: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, Leaflet.js interactive mapping, OpenStreetMap, Nominatim geocoding, Overpass API, and Esri World Dark Gray basemaps.

Creativity & Factors Considered

  • Creativity: Instead of leaving SAR data locked inside complex desktop GIS software for scientists, EchoSphere turns the 12-day "dance" of Earth's shifting rivers into a tactile, visual time-swipe experience paired with real-world emergency SMS delivery.
  • Key Factors Considered: We prioritized low-bandwidth accessibility (lightweight web rendering and offline-capable SMS alerts), linguistic accessibility (plain-Bangla messaging for local comprehension), global applicability (allowing users to analyze any location on Earth), and dual-polarization sensitivity to distinguish standing floodwater from shifting riverbank sediment.
